title: Freya and the Salt Again
premise: Lena Nakamura has survived twenty years in the salt-city of Verrin by carving charms that do nothing and hearing nothing she admits to, since the Purge made magic a hanging offense. When a mute child arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language of the dead Lena secretly hears—she learns the girl's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain by parents desperate to survive a plague Lena's own charms once failed to stop. To free the child before the last dragon-fire gutters out and every soul in the mountain court is extinguished forever, Lena must ally with the magistrate who executed her teacher and descend into a justice older than any law. She wins the child back at the cost of her own memories of the dead who sustained her, choosing an unhaunted future over the comfort of ghosts.
about_author: Elodie Whitlock is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring funerary carvings before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about grief, craft, and the laws people break to stay human.

chapters.title: Charms That Do Nothing
chapters.summary: Lena Nakamura's POV. In her bone-carving shop in outlawed-magic Verrin, Lena sells inert charms to frightened customers while privately hearing the dead murmur in the walls. A routine sale goes wrong when a customer recognizes her teacher's carving style. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on hiding.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. During a curfew storm, a six-year-old girl appears at Lena's door, mute but speaking—when she finally speaks—in the First Tongue, the language of the dead only Lena can hear. The words are a plea: 'They sold me twice.' Emotional beat: terror and recognition; the past knocking loudly.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lena and the ghost of her executed teacher, Maren. Through the dead, Lena learns the child, Isla, is soul-bonded to the court beneath the mountain, where souls are held as currency. Emotional beat: grief repurposed as investigation; the dead as witnesses.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Summons
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corvan Hale's POV introduces him as a man who enforced the Purge and now dreams of voices. He summons Lena on suspicion of unlicensed carving, but his real question is about the child seen entering her shop. Emotional beat: two hunters realizing they may be hunting the same truth.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She hides Isla with a smuggler friend, Ode, and traces the soul-sale contract to a broker called the Tallowman, who buys children's souls for the mountain court. Emotional beat: fury hardening into resolve; survival means becoming dangerous.

chapters.title: The Tallowman's Price
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Tallowman offers information in exchange for a charm carved from Lena's own bone—a piece of herself. She refuses, then watches him sell a mother's grief-memory instead. Emotional beat: horror at what desperation makes legal.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire Guttering
chapters.summary: Maren's ghost POV, deep beneath the city. The last dragon, chained under the mountain, burns low; when it dies, all souls held in the court are extinguished. Isla's soul is among them. Emotional beat: a ticking clock made flesh and flame.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Enemies
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale confronts Lena with evidence, but instead of arresting her, he confesses he executed Maren on false orders and wants absolution or ruin—he no longer cares which. They form a wary pact. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins with confession.

chapters.title: The Road Under the World
chapters.summary: Lena, Hale, and Isla travel the old corpse-roads toward the mountain, guided by the dead, pursued by the Tallowman's hired wardens. Isla speaks her first common word: 'Home?' Emotional beat: found family forming under threat.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They shelter in a village whose inhabitants traded their memories of the plague to the court in exchange for survival—and now cannot say why they feel hollow. Emotional beat: the price of survival made visible; foreshadowing Lena's own choice.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Ford
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Wardens ambush them at a river crossing. Hale reveals himself publicly as a traitor to save Isla, burning his career and reputation. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of change; no way back.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Captured briefly by the Tallowman, Lena reads his ledger and finds her own name—her soul was collateral for Maren's trial twenty years ago. Her invisibility was purchased, not chosen. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing her whole life.

chapters.title: What Maren Knew
chapters.summary: Maren's ghost POV. Maren confesses she bargained Lena's safety away to protect the First Tongue from extinction, believing the child-language must outlive them both. Emotional beat: love that wounds; forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Gates of Bone
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The trio reaches the mountain gate, carved entirely of soul-bone, guarded by a riddle only the First Tongue can answer. Isla, terrified, speaks it aloud. The gate opens. Emotional beat: the smallest member becomes the key.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. Inside, they find the dragon nearly dark and the court of dead bureaucrats trading souls like coin. Hale offers himself as a prisoner to buy time. Emotional beat: awe and dread; law without mercy revealed in full.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Isla's soul comes up for auction. Lena bids the only currency accepted: her memories of the dead, twenty years of voices, including Maren. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible arithmetic—love priced against identity.

chapters.title: Last Light of the Dragon
chapters.summary: Climax. As the dragon gutters, Lena completes the trade, and the freed souls' gratitude rekindles the fire—but the court demands enforcement. Hale breaks the chain binding the dragon, dying in the backlash. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: Ash on the Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The court collapses; souls disperse like embers. Lena carries Isla out but cannot remember why she is crying. Maren's voice is gone. Emotional beat: hollow victory; grief without its object.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Back in Verrin, Lena finds her shop ransacked, her ledger of names burned. Without the dead, her carvings are truly just carvings—and yet customers still come, needing something to hold. Emotional beat: learning to live unhaunted.

chapters.title: Isla Learns to Speak
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Weeks pass; Isla's First Tongue fades as her own soul settles back into her, replaced by ordinary childhood words. Lena teaches her to carve instead. Emotional beat: healing measured in small, ordinary milestones.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ode's POV. Word spreads of the mountain's fall; the city's survivors of soul-sales begin arriving at Lena's door seeking help the law will never give. Lena, reluctantly, becomes their advocate. Emotional beat: purpose reborn from ruin; the personal becomes communal.

chapters.title: Freya and the Salt Again
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue. On the anniversary, Lena and Isla climb to the sea cliffs and carve a small dragon from driftwood bone-white as ash. Lena cannot remember the dead, but she remembers that she loved them. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—memory lost, love retained; the price paid, the life chosen.
